name: AS3320
full_name: Voltage Controlled Filter (VCF), 4-pole architecture pin/electrically compatible with the Curtis CEM3320
description: High-performance four-pole voltage-controlled filter with on-chip voltage-controlled resonance, modern production of the classic Curtis Electromusic Specialties CEM3320. Four independent variable-gain-cell filter sections can be interconnected externally for low-pass, high-pass, band-pass, all-pass, or state-variable/notch responses, and can also be configured as a low-distortion sine-wave VCO. A single VCFI input exponentially controls all four sections' frequency together over a >10-octave range with low feedthrough; a separate resonance path (Vres/Ires) controls Q in a modified-linear manner from zero up to oscillation. Includes an on-chip -2V regulator to keep power dissipation and warm-up drift low.

QFN-24.notes: AS3320F device, 24-lead QFN 4x4mm 0.5mm pitch, per Alfa AS3320 datasheet (2020, rev 8) 'Pin Information' table (p.1, QFN-24L Pin No column) cross-referenced against p.4's mechanical QFN-24 outline drawing (pin 1 indicator, top/bottom view). Only the 18 electrically-defined pins are listed here; QFN pins 1,6,10,13,18,21 are undocumented in this datasheet revision (2020 rev 8) and are omitted rather than guessed. The exposed thermal pad carries a contradictory spec in the source ('Don't connect' in the pin table vs 'improves thermal stability' in the prose) -- see gotchas.

extra.supply (asymmetric): Vcc +9V to +18V; Vee -4V to -18V (not a simple split rail); typ +-15V
extra.current-limiting resistor for Vee: required; REE = (|Vee| - 2.7V) / 8.4mA, e.g. ~1.5k for -15V supply (datasheet Note 3)
extra.frequency control range: 3500:1 min, 10,000:1 typ (>10 octaves), swept over -20mV < VCFI < +160mV
extra.exponential error of frequency control s: 4% typ, 12% max (over -16mV < VCFI < +176mV, most error in upper two octaves)
extra.output noise re max output (LPF, 20kHz c: -76 typ...-86 max dB (table lists -76/-86 as min/typ; more negative = quieter)

typical_application: Classic analog-synth voltage-controlled filter (VCF) core, pin/electrically compatible with the vintage Curtis CEM3320: wire the four independent gain-cell sections externally for low-pass, high-pass, band-pass, notch, all-pass, or state-variable responses, with a shared exponential VCFI frequency control and a separate resonance path capable of driving the filter into self-oscillation (usable as a low-distortion sine VCO). Widely used in Eurorack and boutique synth VCF modules as a modern CEM3320/SSM2040-family second source.
gotchas: negative supply (Vee) always needs a series current-limiting resistor REE; the datasheet gives REE = (|Vee| - 2.7V) / 8.4mA, e.g. ~1.5k for a -15V rail -- omitting it risks exceeding the internal -2V regulator's ratings
supply is asymmetric, not a simple +-V split: Vcc spec'd +9V to +18V while Vee is spec'd -4V to -18V; do not assume a symmetric bipolar supply is required or sufficient

resonance control (Ires/ICR) is untrimmed by default and only specified over 0 to 100uA in the datasheet's own feedthrough test; check the application circuit for the resistor network (Rres, RRI, RRC) needed to reach reliable self-oscillation

QFN (AS3320F) exposed power pad has a genuinely contradictory datasheet: the pin table says 'Don't connect' while the general description says it 'highly improves thermal stability' -- verify against Alfa's own application/eval board or contact them before deciding whether to solder it to a ground/thermal plane
only 18 of the QFN-24's 24 pins are individually named in this datasheet revision (rev 8, 2020); the remaining 6 are not documented and are assumed NC by elimination, not confirmed

pin/electrically intended as a CEM3320-compatible second source (per Alfa's Curtis-lineage AS33xx series and community usage), but this datasheet itself makes no explicit CEM3320 cross-reference claim -- treat the compatibility claim as a well-known community/vendor-lineage fact, not something stated on this PDF
internal -2V regulator node (pin-accessible indirectly via Vee) sits at -2.4 to -2.9V; useful as a quick continuity/power-up sanity check on the negative rail
